Surah Nuh [Meccan; its verses are 28 or 29 in number]

That (we sent him): "Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment" [i.e., with a warning], if they do not believe. A painful punishment, causing pain, in this world and the Hereafter.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 71, verse 2:

﴿He said: "O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner."﴾ Clarifying the warning.

﴿Anna﴾, i.e. that I say to you

Note on the transliteration: ﴿أنْ﴾ is rendered as "Anna" (the verse's own wording is "أن اعبدوا الله" in 71:3, and this gloss explains the particle ﴿أنْ﴾ as introducing the content of the command).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 71, verse 4:

﴿He will forgive you of your sins﴾ "min" (of) is extra (zā'idah), for Islam wipes out what came before it; or it is partitive (tab'īḍiyyah), to exclude the rights of people (ḥuqūq al-'ibād). ﴿And defer you﴾ without punishment ﴿to a specified term﴾, the term of death. ﴿Indeed, the term of Allah﴾, [His punishment for you] if you do not believe, ﴿when it comes, cannot be deferred, if only you knew﴾ that, ﴿you would have believed.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 71, verse 5:

﴿He said, "My Lord, I have invited my people night and day."﴾ That is, constantly, without interruption.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 71 (Nuh), verse 6:

﴿But it only increased them in flight﴾ from faith.

Surah 71, verse 7:

﴿And indeed, every time I called them, that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears﴾ so that they would not hear my words. ﴿and covered themselves with their garments﴾ they covered their heads with them so that they would not look at me. ﴿and persisted﴾ in their disbelief ﴿and became arrogantly proud﴾ they were proud against faith.
Then indeed I called them openly (jihāran), that is, at the top of my voice.
﴿Then I have certainly announced to them﴾ my voice, ﴿and I have spoken to them secretly﴾ the speech.
﴿So I said: "Ask your Lord for forgiveness"﴾ from polytheism (shirk, associating partners with God).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 71, verse 11:

﴿He sends the sky﴾ [i.e., the rain], and they had withheld it, ﴿upon you in abundance﴾ [i.e., abundant in its pouring down].

ﷺ

"And He will provide you with wealth and sons, and make for you gardens and make for you rivers."

Commentary: ﴿and He will provide you with wealth and sons﴾ ... ﴿and make for you gardens﴾ — gardens (jannat): orchards. ﴿and make for you rivers﴾ — flowing rivers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 71, verse 13:

﴿What is the matter with you that you do not hope for dignity from Allah?﴾ That is, you do not expect Allah's dignity toward you, namely that you believe.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 71, verse 14:

﴿While He has created you in stages.﴾ (Aṭwār) is the plural of ṭawr (ṭawr), which means a state or condition: at one stage a drop of sperm (nuṭfah), at another a clinging clot (ʿalaqah), until the human being is fully formed. And reflection upon His creation necessitates belief in its Creator.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 71, verse 15:

﴿Have you not considered﴾ (tarawna) you not look, ﴿how God created seven heavens in layers﴾ one above another.
And the moon as a light within them (i.e., within their totality, which includes the lowest heaven), and made the sun a lamp (sirāj), a shining lamp, and it is stronger than the light of the moon.

Qur'an 71:17 is "And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth like plants."

Here is the translation of the commentary:

﴿And Allah has caused you to grow﴾ — created you — ﴿from the earth﴾ — when He created your father Adam from it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 71, verse 18:

﴿Then He will return you into it﴾ as buried (maqburin), ﴿and bring you out﴾ for the Resurrection (li-l-ba'th).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 71, verse 19:

﴿And Allah has made the earth a spread-out carpet for you﴾ — spread out (mabsutah).
﴿That you may pass along from it roads, spacious highways﴾ — ﴿ṭuruqan﴾ (paths) ﴿fijājan﴾ (wide, open roads).

Noah said: "My Lord, they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children have increased him only in loss" (﴿قالَ نُوح رَبّ إنّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي واتَّبَعُوا﴾). That is, the lowly (al-saflah) and the poor, ﴿مَن لَمْ يَزِدْهُ ماله ووُلْده﴾, "whom neither his wealth nor his children have increased," and they are the leaders, those upon whom blessings were bestowed for that reason. As for "wuld" (walad), it is read with a ḍammah on the waw and a sukūn on the lām, and also with a fatḥah on both. The first (wuld) is said to be the plural of walad with a fatḥah on both, like khushb and khashab; and it is said to have the same meaning, like bukhl and bakhal. ﴿إلّا خَسارًا﴾ means "except loss," that is, rebellion (ṭughyānan) and disbelief (kufran).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 71, verse 22:

﴿And they schemed﴾, i.e., the chiefs, ﴿a tremendous scheme﴾, very great indeed, by denying Nuh and harming him and those who followed him.

And they said [to the common people]: "Do not leave your gods, and do not leave Wadd" (with the waw pronounced with a fatha or a damma), "nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, nor Ya'uq, nor Nasr." These are the names of their idols.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 71, verse 24:

﴿And they have led astray⟩ by them ﴿many⟩ of the people, by commanding them to worship them. ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in misguidance⟩, coordinated with "and they have led astray." He invoked against them when it was revealed to him that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 71, verse 25:

﴿Because of their sins﴾, "mā" (here) is a redundant particle (ṣilah) [added for emphasis]; and in another reading, "khaṭī'ātihim" is read with a hamzah, "khaṭī'ātihim." ﴿They were drowned﴾ by the flood. ﴿And then they were made to enter the Fire﴾, they were punished by it immediately after being drowned beneath the water. ﴿And they found for themselves, besides﴾, i.e., other than, ﴿Allah, no helpers﴾ who could ward off the punishment from them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 71, verse 26:

﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dweller."﴾ That is, "dayyar" means one who dwells in a dwelling (nazil dar), and the meaning is "anyone" (ahadan).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 71, verse 27:

﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants, and they will not beget except a wicked, disbelieving one.﴾ [those who commit wickedness (fujur) and disbelieve (kufr)]. He said that because of what had preceded of the revelation to him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 71, verse 28:

﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾ and they were believers, ﴿and whoever enters my house﴾, my dwelling or my mosque, ﴿as a believer, and the believing men and the believing women﴾ until the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and do not increase the wrongdoers except in ruin﴾, destruction, so they were destroyed.
